title: Exact module pullback: universal ordinary and strict-tower comparisons with evaluation
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be small sites with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and let $(f,c)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi: $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits, and $c:f^{-1}R\to S$. Put $G(M)=f^{-1}M\otimes_{f^{-1}R}S$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ be additive and exact, and $m:G\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ a specified natural isomorphism. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories with localizations $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Write $G^{\mathrm{Tow}},F^{\mathrm{Tow}},m^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ for the levelwise extensions. Let $(L,\epsilon)$ and $(\widetilde L,\tau)$ be specified universal total left-derived pairs for $G$ and $G^{\mathrm{Tow}}$, computed on objectwise K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Write $F_D$ and $F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ for the exact termwise derived descents with localization comparisons $\xi,\Xi$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. All formulas include the exact-localization identifications, and $Q_R^{\mathrm{Tow}},Q_S^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ denote the tower localizations.

There are unique natural isomorphisms $e:L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D$ and $E:\widetilde L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ such that, for every complex $P$ and every complex of strict towers $M$,
$$\xi_Pe_{Q_RP}=Q_S(m_P)\epsilon_P,\qquad \Xi_ME_{Q_R^{\mathrm{Tow}}M}=Q_S^{\mathrm{Tow}}(m^{\mathrm{Tow}}_M)\tau_M.$$
Both $\epsilon_P$ and $\tau_M$ are invertible for every $P,M$. For every $n\geq1$ there is a counit-normalized natural isomorphism $v_n:\operatorname{ev}_n\widetilde L\xrightarrow{\sim}L\operatorname{ev}_n$, characterized on every objectwise K-flat flat-term tower complex $M$ by
$$\epsilon_{M_n}v_{n,Q_R^{\mathrm{Tow}}M}=\operatorname{ev}_n(\tau_M).$$
For every derived strict tower $N$,
$$\operatorname{ev}_n(E_N)=e_{\operatorname{ev}_nN}v_{n,N},$$
where the left side is identified with a map to $F_D\operatorname{ev}_nN$ by exact localization. For every $b\geq a\geq1$, $L(d_{b,a})v_{b,N}=v_{a,N}d'_{b,a}$, where $d,d'$ are the evaluation transition maps on $N,\widetilde L N$. These are assertions in the derived category of strict towers and hold without boundedness assumptions.

proof.text: Write $H=Q_S C(F)$ and $H_G=Q_S C(G)$, and put $\mu=Q_S C(m):H_G\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. The exact-functor theorem makes $(F_D,\xi)$ a right Kan extension of $H$ along $Q_R$. The specified pair $(L,\mu\epsilon)$ is also universal: composing any transformation $TQ_R\to H$ with $\mu^{-1}$, applying the universal property of $(L,\epsilon)$, and composing back gives the required unique factorization. Right Kan uniqueness therefore gives a unique $e:L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D$ with $\xi_P e_{Q_RP}=\mu_P\epsilon_P$. Thus $\epsilon_P=\mu_P^{-1}\xi_P e_{Q_RP}$ is invertible for every complex $P$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, unbounded clause (3) and left-derived dual; universal-pair normalization is the agent-written refinement of the blueprint localization Step 6.

proof.text: Kernels and cokernels of strict towers are levelwise. Hence $F^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ is additive and exact: its kernel and cokernel comparisons at each level are those of exact $F$. Naturality of $m$ at the transition arrows makes its levelwise components a natural tower isomorphism $m^{\mathrm{Tow}}$. Apply the exact-functor theorem to these two abelian tower categories. Composing the specified tower universal counit with $Q_S^{\mathrm{Tow}}C(m^{\mathrm{Tow}})$ preserves universality by the same inverse-composition argument as in Step 1. Right Kan uniqueness gives the unique $E$ with the displayed $\Xi$ equation. Solving that equation for $\tau_M$ proves its invertibility for every tower complex $M$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, unbounded clause (3) and left-derived dual; universal-pair normalization is the agent-written refinement of the blueprint localization Step 6.

proof.text: Exact evaluation descends by the exact-functor factorization theorem. The identity $\operatorname{ev}_n C(F^{\mathrm{Tow}})=C(F)\operatorname{ev}_n$ on tower complexes gives, by localization uniqueness, a natural isomorphism $h_n:\operatorname{ev}_nF_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D\operatorname{ev}_n$. Specify it by $\xi_{M_n}h_{n,QM}=\operatorname{ev}_n(\Xi_M)$, with all evaluation/localization comparisons inserted. Both sides are factorizations of the same functor $M\mapsto Q_S F(M_n)$, which inverts quasi-isomorphisms; clause (2) of localization uniqueness lifts their identity, and its inverse, to this $h_n$. Define the natural isomorphism $w_{n,N}=e_{\operatorname{ev}_nN}^{-1}h_{n,N}\operatorname{ev}_n(E_N)$.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; natural-transformation full faithfulness as stated in lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property, clause (2); agent-written exact-evaluation application.

proof.text: For every tower complex $M$, the equations of Steps 1--3 give $Q_S(m_{M_n})\epsilon_{M_n}w_{n,QM}=\xi_{M_n}h_{n,QM}\operatorname{ev}_n(E_{QM})=\operatorname{ev}_n(\Xi_M E_{QM})=Q_S(m_{M_n})\operatorname{ev}_n(\tau_M)$. Cancel the invertible $Q_S(m_{M_n})$. In particular $w_n$ satisfies the required normalization on the objectwise K-flat flat-term class. Strict diagram K-flat replacements supply this resolving class for the small index $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The normalized tower-evaluation theorem, applied to the present ringed topoi and the specified universal pairs for $G$, gives a unique normalized isomorphism $v_n$ and its transition equations. Consequently $w_n=v_n$; the definition of $w_n$ gives $h_{n,N}\operatorname{ev}_n(E_N)=e_{\operatorname{ev}_nN}v_{n,N}$. Its transition equation is precisely $L(d_{b,a})v_{b,N}=v_{a,N}d'_{b,a}$. All constructions are unbounded.

The 4 steps keep old parent Steps 1-3 (Q80 report lines 51-67) in full, and old Step 3 is made stricter: build h_n by localization (2), set w_n=e^-1 h_n ev_n(E), check the counit normalization, then get w_n=v_n from the uniqueness in lem-cbc-derived-tower-evaluation-normalization. Step 1: (L, Q(m)eps) is again a right Kan extension (bijection by mu^-1). With exact-functor-derived-functor(1) and Kan uniqueness this gives a unique e with xi e = Q(m) eps, so every eps is invertible. Step 2: Tow abelian with levelwise kernels and cokernels, so F^Tow is exact and m^Tow is natural; the same argument gives E and invertible tau. Step 3: M->Q_S F(M_n) inverts quasi-isomorphisms, and I checked the h_n specification map by map. Step 4: chain Q(m)eps w = xi e w = xi h ev(E) = ev(Xi E) = Q(m) ev(tau); cancel Q(m). The cbc node's hypotheses (same small ringed sites, F:=G, K-flat flat-term class from diagram-kflat-replacements) match exactly, and it also gives every b>=a transition. Universality over CoCh vs K(A) is a bijective-on-objects full functor, so no gap. Edge cases checked: F=G with m=id, twisting m, zero objects, b=a, unbounded complexes. No SGA.
